results.note: Work exists (RC 20 = VdGS 4 = Meyer 4, 4 viols Tr T T B, Folop/WIMA edition on IMSLP) but no recording of it identified. The cited NY Consort album's 'Fantasy for Four Viols - No. 4' is programme section 'No. 4, Life', not Coprario's fantasia; MusicBrainz's 47 Coprario recordings hold no 4-part fantasia. Keep only if a recording or concert is found.
IMSLP file names call it 'Io son ferito amore', VdGS a5 No. 2 (RC 24=VdGS 1, RC 26=VdGS 3); Hathor Consort (Ramée 2022) plays 'Fantasia No. 2' 2:55 right after Palestrina's Io son ferito, ahi lasso.

IMSLP lists exactly 3 fantasias (RC 122, 123, U 7), 7 almains (RC 124, U 8, 125, 126, U 9, 127, 128) and the corant RC 129. Savall/Coin/Casademunt (Astree 1989) record 5 almaines and the coranto (17:51), so the set is only partly recorded.

IMSLP's '2 viols and organ' (treble + bass viol) is the same scoring: Christ Church Mus. 411-13 and Hoffmann's catalogue give 'violin, bass viol and organ' for Charteris 93-108 (RC 93 = G minor). Globe recording 'Fantasia Suite No. 1 in G Minor' 8:19 (recorder for violin).
RC 94 = VdGS 2, G minor, violin/bass viol/organ per Christ Church and Hoffmann (IMSLP's '2 viols and organ' is the treble-viol reading). Globe 'Fantasia Suite No. 2 in G Minor' 8:24.
Christ Church: Charteris 101 = VdGS 9, C major. MusicBrainz titles the Marq/Hantai/Le Concert Francais (Auvidis 1992) track 'Suite en Do majeur No. 9' (4:23+1:38+1:17 = 7:18).
Christ Church: Charteris 104 = VdGS 12, D minor. MusicBrainz titles the Marq/Hantai (Auvidis 1992) track 'Suite en Re mineur No. 12' (4:37+1:59+2:00 = 8:36).

IMSLP: No. 12 for 2 violins (or oboe, trumpet), cello/viol, continuo; Op. 1 dated 1700 (Wikipedia). Friedrich/Capriccio 2002 (C major, 6:33) and Spiritato!/Delphian 2020 (trumpet and oboe, 6:46) record it.
D minor, four movements Grave-Allegro-Adagio-Allegro, 5:11-6:25 across Avison, London Baroque, Chandos, Brilliant recordings.
E major; Preludio, Allemanda, Sarabanda, Corrente as in IMSLP; Avison Ensemble (Linn 2013) 5:54.

Marx WoO 4 'a tromba sola, due violini e basso' (Brilliant 5:33, five movements; Naxos Interpreti Veneziani 6:40). IMSLP lists oboe first with trumpet as the alternative; trumpet-first is right for the Marx edition and the recordings.

WoO 5-10 were published together as 6 Sonate a tre (Amsterdam 1714); the siblings WoO 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 already carry 1714, only WoO 7 is blank. Recorded by Musica Amphion (5:05) and Ensemble Aurora (6:08), D major, four movements.
G minor, four movements, Ensemble Aurora/Gatti (Arcana 1998) 5:55; Marx urtext edition (Arno Volk 1976); 1714 Amsterdam print of WoO 5-10.

Five movements (Prelude, Scherzo, Nocturne, Fugue, Postlude); Corigliano Quartet (Naxos) 32:19, Cleveland Quartet (Telarc) 34:16. Naxos titles it 'String Quartet No. 1, Farewell'; Wikipedia gives the 1997 Grammy.
Corigliano Quartet (Naxos 2007) 5:27; composer's list dates it 2003.

fixes.notes: The composer's 2003 quartet arrangement of his 1972 chorus on a Richard Wilbur poem; about three minutes

results.note: Only recording found (Corigliano Quartet, Naxos) runs 2:54, not about 2 min. Arrangement by the composer (2003 from the 1972 chorus) confirmed on his site and Wikipedia.
Composer's list: Soliloquy for clarinet and string quartet (1977), adapted from the Clarinet Concerto; Tesla Quartet/Fiterstein (Orchid 2019) 8:32.

Composer's site lists the tenor version with flute, oboe, clarinet, harpsichord and string quartet (9 players, 1970; chamber-orchestra version 1999/2003). The RCA recording (1978 LP, Gold Seal CD 1990, Robert White, 17:10) is the 8-instrument version: it predates the 1999 orchestral version and a search result credits Nyfenger, Lucarelli, Rabbai, American String Quartet, Peress.
IMSLP: 3 flutes, oboes or violins + continuo, first part also musette/vielle/recorder, G minor, 1732. Only recording found is Concerto Zampogna (primTON, hurdy-gurdy lead) 4:01.
C minor-C major, four movements; Stradivaria/Cuiller (Ades 1996) 6:06, Concerto Zampogna 5:07. No dated print found, 'c. 1732' is an inference between No. 2 (1732) and No. 4 (1733).
A major, 3 movements, 'en quatuor' for 3 flutes or violins + bass, first part also musette; Arion (2008) 5:28. Only the Arion recording found.

IMSLP's 'flute, oboe, violin' only spells out the print's 'flutes, hautbois, violons'; its own line says 'or 3 treble instruments, continuo', so 3 violins + continuo holds. Cafe Zimmermann (Alpha 2008) 5:56.
G major, 3 flutes/oboes/violins + continuo, first part also musette/vielle/recorder (IMSLP); Ensemble Meridiana (Chandos 2016) 4:52.
IMSLP lists No. 10 'Ma mie Margo' (1735); Stradivaria/Cuiller (Ades 1996) three movements, 4:31.
Print: first part for cors de chasse, musette, vielle, flute or violin, + 2 violins + bass; C major (Stradivaria 'en Ut majeur'), 5:53; 1741 per IMSLP list.
Only change: minutes was blank; the concerto track on Stradivaria/Cuiller (Ades 1996) is 2:18. Print is for three violins + bass, 1743 (IMSLP).
IMSLP: 'La Turque et la Confession' (1749-50), no. 19; Arion (2008) 'La Turque' 4:23, three movements, A major. Only the Arion recording found.
IMSLP: ca. 1773, three tunes beginning with La Marche du Huron; Arion 7:13 and Cafe Zimmermann 7:14, C major.
IMSLP: 3 movements for musettes, vielles, flutes or violins + continuo; Les Musiciens de Mademoiselle de Guise (Bayard 2002) 5:58.
Op. 4 (1728 or before) for flutes/violins/oboes + bass; Stradivaria/Cuiller (Ades 1996) 'Concerto pour traverso en mi mineur, op. 4 no. 6' 7:37.

IMSLP: 4 viols/cellos/bassoons or 3 bass instruments + continuo, D major, 9 min. Recorded on viols by Ricercar Consort (7:50), Springfels (9:44), Musica Franca (9:09) and by four bassoons (Arion/Fiat, 8:23).

Print: violin or flute, violin, viola, figured bass. La Fantasia (Brilliant, conducted by Voskuilen) 8:36, El Afecto Ilustrado (2021) 8:17. Whether any recording is one to a part is not shown, see chunk note.
D major in Arion and El Afecto Ilustrado; three noels, 6:45-7:44 across three recordings, entry 8 is fine.
Eight noels; La Fantasia 13:55, El Afecto Ilustrado 14:26. Key left out of the title is right to leave out: only El Afecto gives one (G major).
D minor in Arion and El Afecto Ilustrado; seven noels, 9:27-11:10 across the three recordings.
Key conflict: Arion gives 'No. 5 in A minor', El Afecto Ilustrado 'Symphony 5 in E Minor'; IMSLP gives no key. Drop the unconfirmed key from the title. Eight noels, 13:16-14:16 (entry 14 fine).
A major in Arion and El Afecto Ilustrado; four noels, 6:25-7:22.

Tre Gran Trio for clarinet, cello and piano, Op. 56/60/63 (Italian Wikipedia, Da Vinci notes); Trio Clementi (Da Vinci Classics 2021) 16:36; Musicart Trio also records Op. 56. Corticelli (Bologna 1804-1840), pupil of Mattei; trios published posthumously 1842 by Lucca (year blank in the entry).
Clarinet, cello, piano, Op. 60 'Genere fantastico'; Trio Clementi (Da Vinci Classics 2021) 16:57; published posthumously 1842 (Lucca), per Da Vinci notes.
Clarinet, cello, piano, Op. 63 'Genere religioso'; Trio Clementi (Da Vinci Classics 2021) 13:46; published posthumously 1842 (Lucca), per Da Vinci notes.

fixes.notes: Homage to Bellini's melodies for flute, cello and piano; Trio Clementi play it on clarinet

results.note: Op. 55 is for flute, cello and piano (Italian Wikipedia; Da Vinci album notes: 'original score was for flute, cello and piano'). Only the Trio Clementi recording (clarinet in the flute part, 6:13) was found, so the clarinet version may be a performer's adaptation. Formation stays winds-strings, players 3.
Printed 1725, 2 violins (or flutes) + continuo with separate basse d'archet and continuo parts (folded into continuo); 14 numbers; Gli Incogniti/Beyer 28:28, Arcangelo/Cohen 31:56.

IMSLP: 1916, 5:30, alt. title 'Pedantic Quartet', published 1965. IMSLP lists three sections (Andante sostenuto, Allegro non troppo, Andante); Mode splits it into two movements, Andante sostenuto-Allegro non troppo (4:10) and Andante (1:46), so 'two movements' stands.

fixes.notes: Four movements; Cowell later made a harp version (1962)

results.note: The cited Mode recording is Cowell's separate 1962 harp version (3:18+5:34+3:20+1:56 = 14:08), not this work. Harpsichord original: 1954 (Wise/AMP; IMSLP), 12 min (Wise), IMSLP 11 min; Continuum/Cheryl Seltzer/Sachs (Naxos 2005, Apple 60621477, four movements) 11:06. The harp version is not catalogued.
Kronos 'Quartet Euphometric (1916-1919)' 1:50; Colorado Quartet (Mode 1999) 2:09.
IMSLP VdGS No. 1, Tr Tr T B; LeStrange Viols (New Focus FCR905, 2015) 'Fantasia a 4 No. 1' 2:28.
IMSLP VdGS No. 2, Tr Tr T B; LeStrange Viols 2:52.

note: Corrette's six Symphonies de Noëls (101788-101793): the print is a quartet (violin or flute, violin, viola, figured bass) but 'exécutables à grand orchestre'; La Fantasia (Brilliant) is credited as 'performing orchestra' under Voskuilen and Arion is an orchestre baroque; El Afecto Ilustrado (La Cúpula 2021) may be one to a part but I could not confirm it, so the scope is unproven. Coprario RC 20 (100399) has no identified recording. Corticelli Op. 55 (106006) is flute, not clarinet. Cowell HC 802: the cited Mode disc is the harp version.
